title: Impact of US and China Protectionist Measures on Singapore’s Economy
what_it_is: Impact of US and China Protectionist Measures on Singapore’s Economy

sections.label: US-China tariffs impact Singapore exports
sections.summary: MTI estimates US and China tariffs directly affect about 0.09% of Singapore's domestic exports, a limited impact given affected products' modest share.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: To date, the direct negative impact of the tariffs announced by the US and China on the Singapore economy is limited, given the modest share that the affected products have as a percentage of Singapore's total domestic exports.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Trade and Industry's (MTI's) analysis estimates the tariffs to directly impact about 0.09% of our domestic exports to the world.

sections.label: Singapore engages US and China on tariffs
sections.summary: Singapore registered concerns with US and Chinese departments, supports free trade and rules-based multilateralism, and worries escalating unilateral tariffs will hurt global supply chains.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Singapore has also registered our concerns with the relevant US and Chinese departments and is continuing to engage them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Singapore is a strong proponent of free trade and supporter of the rules-based multilateral trading system.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We remain concerned that an escalating cycle of expanding unilateral tariff measures will result in negative spillover effects on global supply chains.

sections.label: Study of long trade war implications
sections.summary: MTI staff and economists were asked to study a drawn-out or escalating trade war's direct, indirect and third-country effects on Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: So, that is the first order of business.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: I have also asked MTI staff and economists to do an in-depth study of the possible implications of a long drawn out trade war or an escalating trade war.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The first level of implication is that if the tariff goes up on specific products, there is a direct impact on the cost of business, the cost of the factories, companies and so forth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But there is also an indirect impact, which is, even though the tariffs are not targeted at Singapore, it will cause the global trade flows to shift.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: And when the global trade flows shift, it will have a knock-on impact on Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Whether it is positive, negative, to what extent, we will need to study this carefully.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: There is yet a third impact because when the tariffs are targeted even at third-party countries, it affects the trade flows between and amongst these countries, which will then have yet another round of consequent effects on Singapore.
